gaps.quote: which may be taken to be $2$
gaps.note: Wrong. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear, line 1396-1397) requires a fixed ODD prime q, and the bit network's edge matrix 2P_{U_a} (line 1164) has numerator 2, so q=2 would divide a numerator and the factors would not stay invertible mod q. q must avoid all denominators and diagonal numerators of the matrices, so it cannot be taken to be 2.

gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: Does not follow from the previous sentence, which only requires q not to divide denominators. Also false as stated, since a zero entry has numerator 0, which q divides. The paper (lines 1411-1413) requires q to avoid every denominator and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor, so that the triangular factors stay invertible mod q; the page never gives this reason.

gaps.quote: The paper cites this factorization from earlier work without proof
gaps.note: Inconsistent with the paper: Lemma lower-lower (lines 1364-1392) states the factorization and gives its elementary elimination proof; Grigor'ev is credited only for the Bruhat factorization it is adapted from (line 1360-1362). The paper proves it, not merely cites it.

The reader is not told what a negative source projection, a decreasing edge or the dimension lost on one is, nor what the rank budget counts, so the identity and the inequality N>2L_b cannot be interpreted. The citation lets them check, but the page does not say what these objects are or why the inequality holds.

gaps.quote: which the recurrence turns into a saving of a power of the chunk width (the chunk length)
gaps.note: No recurrence is stated on this page, and chunk width and the recursion in which the interchanges are called recursively are not defined, so the reader cannot see how fewer than R interchanges per wire gives a power saving.
